name: Omani Shuwa
description: Marinated goat or lamb slow-cooked for 24 to 48 hours in a sealed underground pit oven (Tanour). Wrapped in banana or date palm leaves and seasoned with vinegar, garlic, coriander, and Omani spice blend.
ingredients_summary: goat meat, garlic, vinegar, coriander, cumin, chili, cloves, date palm leaves
cooking_method: Pit-roasted underground over hot embers for 24-48 hours
cultural_notes: Centerpiece of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha celebrations across the Sultanate.

name: Majboos
description: Fragrant basmati rice infused with saffron, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, and black dried lime (Loomi), layered with slow-simmered chicken or lamb.
ingredients_summary: basmati rice, chicken, dried black lime, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, onions, garlic, saffron
cooking_method: Simmered spiced broth absorbed into parboiled rice
cultural_notes: Served as a welcoming hospitality feast for guests and Friday family lunches.

name: Harees
description: A comforting, velvety porridge of whole cracked wheat slow-cooked with tender shredded beef or chicken and beaten vigorously with an Omani wooden paddle (Mضراب), topped with melted local ghee.
ingredients_summary: coarse wheat grains, chicken or beef, local ghee, salt, cinnamon
cooking_method: Slow-simmered and beaten until uniform porridge consistency
cultural_notes: A quintessential staple of Ramadan iftar tables and community gatherings.

name: Omani Halwa
description: World-famous Omani confection simmered for hours in large copper cauldrons (Mirjal). Made from tapioca starch, clarified butter, caramelized sugar, saffron, crushed cardamom, rose water from Jebel Akhdar, and almonds.
ingredients_summary: sugar, cornstarch, ghee, rosewater, saffron, cardamom, roasted almonds, cashews
cooking_method: Continuous high-heat reduction and stirring in large copper cauldrons
cultural_notes: The primary symbol of Omani hospitality; universally served alongside hot bitter Omani Kahwa.

name: Mashuai
description: Spit-roasted or baked whole Kingfish seasoned with ground coriander, turmeric, and sea salt, served alongside a savory turmeric-lemon basmati rice with Loomi sauce.
ingredients_summary: whole kingfish, basmati rice, turmeric, lemons, loomi, coriander, garlic
cooking_method: Open flame spit-roast or oven-baked, served with spiced citrus rice
cultural_notes: Signature coastal delicacy from Sur, Quriyat, and the Al Batinah fishing communities.

name: Mishkak
description: Tender skewers of marinated beef, mutton, or chicken grilled over red-hot charcoal on seaside promenades. Basted continuously with spicy-sour tamarind garlic dip (Tamarhindi sauce).
ingredients_summary: beef or mutton cubes, tamarind paste, garlic, black pepper, chili, vinegar, cumin
cultural_notes: The king of Omani street food, heavily popular at night on beaches and roadside souqs.

name: Madrouba
description: A savory porridge of beaten rice and shredded tender chicken simmered with tomatoes, aromatic dried lime, ginger, and turmeric until thick and creamy.
ingredients_summary: rice, chicken, tomatoes, dried lime, onion, ginger, turmeric, ghee
cooking_method: Long braise beaten with a wooden spoon into a savory puree
cultural_notes: Cherished winter comfort food across the northern and peninsula regions.

name: Paplou
description: A spicy, citrusy yellow coastal broth made with fresh kingfish or tuna steaks, whole garlic cloves, crushed black peppercorns, turmeric, and sour green mango or dried lime juice.
ingredients_summary: fresh tuna or kingfish, turmeric, black lime, green mango, garlic, chili, fresh coriander
cooking_method: Quick rolling boil to keep fish tender and broth vibrant
cultural_notes: A traditional fisherman's soup designed to invigorate, served hot alongside plain white rice.

name: Khubz Ragag
description: Wafer-thin, ultra-crispy unleavened flatbread quickly spread over a blazing domed iron griddle (Tawa). Often folded hot with spreadable processed cheese, raw egg, honey, or spicy Omani chips.
ingredients_summary: wheat flour, water, salt, optional cheese and honey
cooking_method: Rapid griddle baking on a convex iron plate
cultural_notes: An everyday staple breakfast and dinner bread freshly made in Omani households.

name: Omani Kahwa
description: Traditional lightly roasted Arabica coffee brewed with freshly ground green cardamom pods, saffron threads, and sometimes rose water. Served unsweetened in tiny cups (Finjan).
ingredients_summary: lightly roasted coffee beans, cardamom, saffron, rose water
cooking_method: Decoction boiled in an ornate traditional Dallah pot
cultural_notes: An indispensable ritual of welcome in every Omani Majlis; served continuously with fresh dates.
